data.description:
## Status
PLACEHOLDER — not yet brainstormed. This epic captures research scope only; decomposition requires a `/dso:brainstorm` session.

## Context
`w21-bsnz` (Create a process to remediate legacy code) ships a `/dso:remediate` skill scoped to *deletion-class* bloat: dead code, unused locals, duplicate test bodies, import-only files, broken doc links, etc. Mapped against the classical refactoring catalog (https://refactoring.guru/refactoring/catalog), that scope sits almost entirely inside the **Dispensables** smell family.

This epic extends the same two-agent pipeline (blue-team filter + resolver, gated by `/dso:review`) to the four remaining smell families, which require *transformation* actions rather than deletion.

## Reference
- Refactoring Catalog: https://refactoring.guru/refactoring/catalog
- Smell families (Fowler/Beck): Bloaters, Object-Orientation Abusers, Change Preventers, Dispensables (covered by w21-bsnz), Couplers
- ~70 named refactorings organized into 6 technique groups (Composing Methods, Moving Features Between Objects, Organizing Data, Simplifying Conditional Expressions, Simplifying Method Calls, Dealing with Generalization)

## In-Scope Smell Families (to be refined during brainstorm)

**Bloaters** — Long Method, Large Class, Long Parameter List, Primitive Obsession, Data Clumps
- Primary refactorings: Extract Method, Extract Class, Introduce Parameter Object, Replace Data Value with Object

**Couplers** — Feature Envy, Inappropriate Intimacy, Message Chains, Middle Man
- Primary refactorings: Move Method, Hide Delegate, Remove Middle Man, Extract Class

**Object-Orientation Abusers** — Switch Statements, Temporary Field, Refused Bequest, Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
- Primary refactorings: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism, Replace Type Code with Subclasses/State, Push Down Method/Field

**Change Preventers** — Divergent Change, Shotgun Surgery, Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
- Primary refactorings: Extract Class, Move Method/Field, Inline Class

**Residual Dispensables (not covered by w21-bsnz)** — Speculative Generality, Data Class, Comments-that-explain-what (overlaps CLAUDE.md "no comments by default" rule), Lazy Class

## Interaction with w21-bsnz

This epic is **blocked by w21-bsnz** because it depends on three w21-bsnz deliverables as a foundation:

1. **Two-agent pipeline** (`dso:bloat-blue-team` → `dso:bloat-resolver` → `/dso:review`). Transformations are higher blast radius than deletions; the existing pipeline is the right place to add them.

2. **Confidence map YAML** (`plugins/dso/config/remediate-confidence-map.yaml`). This epic will extend the schema to `{smell_family, refactoring, engine} → confidence` so every catalog smell can be routed through the same three-tier auto/blue-team/skip logic.

3. **Resolver action enum**. Currently `{delete_function, delete_file, delete_block, annotate, flag}` — deletion-only. This epic will extend the enum with transformation actions:
   - `extract_method`, `extract_class`, `inline_method`, `inline_class`
   - `move_method`, `move_field`
   - `introduce_parameter_object`
   - `replace_conditional_with_polymorphism`
   - `replace_nested_conditional_with_guard_clauses` (candidate bright-line — mechanically detectable)
   - `pull_up_method`, `push_down_method`
   - `rename_method`
   (Note: `refactor_remove_param` is already proposed as an inbound addition to w21-bsnz from epic bc7f-1a0d; this epic generalizes that pattern.)

## New Architectural Deliverable

**Per-refactoring preconditions registry** (`plugins/dso/config/refactoring-preconditions.yaml`). Each catalog refactoring has well-defined preconditions (Move Method: no parameter mutation; Extract Method: preserve return type; Pull Up Field: identical type across subclasses). This registry powers the resolver's existing `cascade-check` HARD-GATE and populates `NO_CHANGE: CASCADE_RISK` rationale categories with structured precondition violations rather than free-text reasons.

## Open Questions for Brainstorm

- Granularity: one epic covering all four families, or split per family?
- Bright-line candidates: are any catalog refactorings mechanically safe enough for auto-remediation (e.g., Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses)? Most are inherently judgment-class.
- Detection engines: which open-source tools cover Bloaters/Couplers detection (SonarQube, CodeClimate, radon, jscpd, eslint complexity rules)?
- Multi-stack coverage: which refactorings are feasible across Python/JS/TS/Ruby vs. require stack-specific resolvers?
- Integration with `prior-art-search` (`plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/prior-art-search.md`): catalog vocabulary should be referenced when proposing new abstractions.

## Out of Scope (for now)
- New language stack support (inherits w21-bsnz coverage: Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Markdown)
- Mutation-testing-based detection (too slow for the commit gate, per w21-bsnz research)
- Behavior-preserving formal verification of refactorings (relies on the review gate + test suite as proxy)

## Related Epics
- `w21-bsnz` — Create a process to remediate legacy code (BLOCKER — foundational pipeline + YAML schema + action enum)
- `bc7f-1a0d` — Cross-file static bloat detectors (sibling — extends w21-bsnz with cross-file probabilistic patterns; this epic extends w21-bsnz with transformation actions)
